organization.name: The Moon Society
organization.tagline: Building a spacefaring civilization on the Moon.
organization.mission: The Moon Society is a membership-based space advocacy organization dedicated to furthering the development and settlement of the Moon. We bring together citizens, scientists, engineers, and enthusiasts who believe that a permanent human presence on the Moon is both achievable and essential.

primary.name: Gold
primary.usage: Primary accent, calls to action, highlights

secondary.name: Blue
secondary.usage: Mid-tone blue for depth and layering

neutral.name: Cool Gray 2
neutral.usage: Subtle borders, dividers on dark mode

neutral.name: Cool Gray 11
neutral.usage: Borders and dividers on light backgrounds

neutral.name: Near-Black
neutral.usage: Deep background, slightly warmer than pure black

neutral.name: Black
neutral.usage: Use sparingly; prefer Near-Black for large areas

semantic.name: Warning
semantic.usage: Warnings and caution indicators (Dark Gold). FILL/ICON color only — at 2.4:1 on white it FAILS WCAG for text; never use as body text on light backgrounds. For warning text on light, pair with a dark foreground or use on a dark surface.

extended.name: Light Gold
extended.usage: Lighter gold variant for gradients or hover states

extended.name: Dark Gold
extended.usage: Darker gold variant for text on light backgrounds

extended.name: Brownish Gold
extended.usage: Warm accent for editorial or print applications

extended.name: Grayish Brown
extended.usage: Warm neutral for text or accents

extended.name: Pinkish Off-White
extended.usage: Soft warm background for special sections

fonts.usage: Hero/display headlines, event titles, large promotional text (32px and above). Same family as headings — display vs. heading is a weight/size distinction, not a different typeface. Prefer 800. Replaces the former Syne display face (retired in the 2026 direction; see moonsociety.org).
Section headings (H1–H6), navigation labels, button text. Prefer 600–700.
Paragraph text, list items, form labels, captions, general reading text. 16–18px, line-height 1.5–1.6.

Long-form editorial content, pull quotes, formal documents, print publications. Loaded via Google Fonts CDN. Replaces the former Palatino / TeX Gyre Pagella system-serif stack as part of the 2026 move to CDN-delivered Google Fonts (no system or self-hosted faces).
Code samples, technical specifications, fixed-width data, terminal references. Use sparingly.

tokens.$comment: Design tokens beyond color and font family. Mirrors the live theme (moonsociety.org) :root. This is the single source — colors.css, tokens.json, and colors.json are GENERATED from this file by scripts/generate-derived.mjs. Do not hand-edit the derived files.

wider.usage: Wide uppercase labels and section markers

card.usage: Default card / surface elevation on the dark brand background

primary-white.description: Primary web and print logo. White text, lunar disc on transparent background. Use for website headers, slides, and any dark-background placement.

primary-black.description: Primary light-background logo. Black text, lunar disc on transparent background. 440x190px, web-optimized.

primary-black-print.description: Black text wordmark on transparent background. High resolution, suitable for print.

icon.description: Small thumbnail version of the white-text wordmark. Suitable for favicons or very small placements only.

email-black.description: White text wordmark on solid black background. Use only where the background is exactly black (e.g. email templates). 440x190px.

canonical-raster.description: CANONICAL raster logo (2026 re-upload, 1580×646 PNG, transparent background). This exact asset is the site-wide header/footer lockup on www.moonsociety.org as of 2026-07-06 — use it for any raster placement instead of the legacy PNG/JPG exports below. For vector contexts use canonical-svg.

canonical-svg.description: CANONICAL Moon Society wordmark. Vector source of truth — use this for the logo wherever SVG is supported, and to generate any new raster sizes. White wordmark with lunar disc, designed for dark backgrounds. Does NOT render a visible trademark (TM) glyph; the raster variants that include a TM are legacy and non-canonical.

face-only.description: Lunar disc / face-only mark (no wordmark). Use for favicons, avatars, and small icon placements.

vector-source.description: Original 2014 vector artwork with full metadata. Historical source for reproduction; prefer canonical-svg for current use.

rules.clearSpace: Minimum clear space equal to the height of the capital 'T' in 'THE' on all sides.
prohibitions: Do not alter the proportions or spacing of the wordmark
Do not change the colors of any element within the logo
Do not add effects such as drop shadows, outlines, glows, or gradients
Do not rotate or skew the logo
Do not place the logo on backgrounds that reduce legibility
Do not crop or partially obscure the lunar disc
Use the canonical SVG wordmark, which does not render a visible trademark (TM) glyph; do not add a TM to it or substitute the legacy TM-bearing raster files

voice.coreStatement: The Moon Society's voice conveys credible enthusiasm. We are technically informed but never exclusionary, optimistic about humanity's future on the Moon but grounded in real engineering, science, and policy. We sound like a knowledgeable colleague who is genuinely excited about what they do and wants you to be part of it.
do: Be authoritative, not academic — use precise language without unnecessary jargon
Be aspirational, not fantastical — advocate for real missions, technology, and timelines
Be inclusive, not insider — welcome people who discovered us yesterday
Be active, not passive — use language that reflects agency and momentum
Provide enough context that a motivated newcomer can follow technical terms
dont: Overuse 'lunar' as a modifier when 'Moon' works fine
Use sci-fi cliches ('boldly go', 'final frontier', 'to the stars')
Use insider shorthand in public-facing text (MMM, LDC, WSD without explanation)

ldc.name: LDC 2026
ldc.tagline: The premier virtual conference on permanent lunar settlement.
ldc.description: The Moon Society's annual conference series bringing together the global community working toward a permanent human presence on the Moon. LDC 2026 focuses on the surface and subsurface of the Moon, from geology and resource extraction to habitat design and human factors.
ldc.theme: Surface and subsurface of the Moon
ldc.inherits: Uses the parent Moon Society color palette and typography system as its baseline while maintaining its own conference identity mark.

lunarpedia.name: Lunarpedia
lunarpedia.tagline: A resource for reaching our stepping stone to the Solar System.
lunarpedia.description: The Moon Society's open, collaborative MediaWiki encyclopedia documenting everything needed to set up self-sustaining lunar bases and colonies — engineering, science, designs, and business models.
lunarpedia.platform: MediaWiki 1.43.x LTS (live); canonical skin: Vector 2022 (vector-2022) with Codex day/night/auto color modes

readingSurface.note: Adopts canonical Vector 2022 / WikimediaUI (Codex) tokens for the reading experience; Moon Society palette is reserved for brand chrome (footer, cross-links, campaigns).

typography.body: system sans stack (-apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif); Noto Sans acceptable substitute

lunarpedia.inherits: Inherits Moon Society voice and brand accents (Space Cadet Blue, Gold) for chrome only; the article reading surface follows canonical Vector 2022, and article link colors stay wiki-standard rather than brand Cerulean.

mmm.name: Moon Miners' Manifesto
mmm.tagline: The Moon Society's lunar settlement journal — publishing since 1986.
mmm.description: Founded and long edited by Peter Kokh, Moon Miners' Manifesto is the Society's flagship publication: four decades of essays and designs on lunar habitats, ISRU, settlement planning, and space development. The full archive (1986–present) is published online at moonmanifesto.com, organized by category (Announcements, Designs, Discussion, Habitats, History, In Focus, News, Planning, Reports) with cross-links to The Moon Society, Lunarpedia, and Luna City Press. Copyright 1986–present by Moon Society Incorporated and other parties; 'Moon Miners' Manifesto' is a Moon Society trademark.
mmm.platform: WordPress; custom theme 'Corolis' (WP theme header currently reads 'Crocco for MMM' v0.4, by James Gholston, public domain / CC0). CSS Grid layout with deliberate inline-block and float fallbacks — designed to be 'highly shatter-resistant' on legacy browsers. moonmanifesto.org 301-redirects to moonmanifesto.com.

readingSurface.note: Light editorial reading surface built from the parent palette plus MMM's own warm 'regolith' neutrals. Masthead art and category badges carry the visual identity; body pages stay newspaper-plain.

typography.headings: Spartan MB (self-hosted webfont; the League Spartan precursor) — visually continuous with the parent brand's League Spartan
typography.body: Noto Sans (matches parent brand body face)
typography.serif: Palatino stack for editorial passages (legacy: the parent brand has since moved its serif to Spectral; MMM retains Palatino for archival continuity)

mmm.inherits: Uses the full Moon Society core palette (Space Cadet Blue, Gold, Blue, Cerulean, Cyan) and the Spartan/Noto Sans/Inconsolata type system on a light reading surface, extended with MMM-specific warm regolith neutrals (#453536, #C1B2B6, #968C83) and its own masthead art. The archive predates the 2026 brand system; treat its palette additions as sub-brand-local, not parent tokens.

versioned.note: Immutable, version-pinned snapshots. The unversioned URLs above always track the latest brand release; pin these /v2/ paths so a downstream pipeline does not break on the next brand update. The major version matches the brand.json major (currently 2).
